text.p: The following are top stories from selected Singapore newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Dozens of Hindu worshippers die when fire breaks out in 11th-century temple in southern India and sets off stampede among panic-stricken devotees, authorities say.
- United States and Japan outline proposed defence guidelines that would allow them to plan together to defend Japan against attack and respond to crises in the region.
- Prime Minister Goh Chok Tong will visit Philippines from Monday to Wednesday at invitation of President Fidel Ramos.
- Singapore General Hospital confirms head of obstetrics and gynaecology department, Dr Maurine Tsakok, suspended from all duties since Friday.
- Revenues of many of region's new telecom operators will surpass those of older counterparts by year 2000 as new players adopt more aggressive marketing and pricing strategies.

- New York Cotton Exchange defers planned launch of first-ever Singapore-dollar futures contract after Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) voices concern to U.S. regulators over the unwelcome internationalisation of currency.

- New telecommunications operators in Asia beginning to have "significant impact" on region's telecoms market, with most of those from developing countries growing faster than incumbents, says report by International Telecommunication Union.
- DBS Land subsidiary Raffles Holdings buys one of London's most historic hotels, 118-room Brown's Hotel.
- Expatriate Indian socialities in Hongkong stashing extravagant jewellery in Singapore bank vaults amid fears China could crack down on gem and gold exports after July 1, report says.
- Listed retailers expected to see improved earnings this year after trimming operations to battle poor retail climate.
- Creative Technology announces worldwide marketing campaign costing over Singapore $71.5 million to encourage acceptance of its latest 640 voice Sound Blaster line of products.
